content.text: The indemnity package meets — and in places exceeds — the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 satisfies the preferred position in full. 20.1 gives an unqualified Vendor IP infringement defence and indemnity covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel, with no modification/combination/specification exclusions (better than the fallback). 20.2 adds Vendor indemnities for breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud — matching model language (a)–(d) and adding injury cover. 20.4 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-limited notice failure, and settlement consent protections). 20.5 provides the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services. Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 stays appropriately narrow — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with express carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or Vendor instructions. Indemnification obligations are also "Excluded Claims" under 21.3, so they sit outside the 21.1 cap and the 21.2 consequential-damages waiver; no 3× super-cap compromise is needed. Nothing here requires a redline.
